checks: The differences of the base-and-label vertices first span the n base axes and then the k label axes after subtracting their base parts. Vertex differences within groups span the rD independent active-block axes. Thus there are n+k+rD=r(D+1)−1 independent differences.

The real base projection is the unit cube. Every binary vertex is exposed, so only its group contributes to that sampled fiber. The finite disjoint union of congruent D-faces has intrinsic dimension D and equal normalized intrinsic mass per face.

Continuous box thickening commutes with taking an integer fiber. The active simplex neighborhood times shrinking intervals gives equal positive d-volume at every base. Continuity from above of active-set volume and uniform continuity of test functions on the common compact support prove the asserted weak limit.

For moving marks and fixed nonzero normal, through-mark caps are contained eventually in the fixed η-enlarged closed cap. Weak convergence bounds the limsup by its closed mass, and continuity from above yields the closed limiting trace. Upper semicontinuity for the fixed laws and the common compact bound permit a subsequence of maximizers. Strict separation gives zero depth outside the convex support.

Both Γ_D and Γ_d tend to 1/e for fixed n as D tends to infinity. Their ratio tends to one, so a fixed c>1 gives a strict comparison for some finite D and hence for all small enough positive thicknesses.
